title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): Let go of the outcome, hold on to the work; self-doubt as a sign you care
summary: Andreea Popa recounts a March in which Thunder's SXSW event in Austin drew 7 of 70 sign-ups, then Berlin and a home Thunder Talks on self-doubt. She reports Cris opened that talk framing self-doubt as caring and preparing, not something to fight. The post argues for staying in the process, learning rooms by being in them, and treating culture as behaviour.

principles.text: Self-doubt can signal that you care and are ready to prepare and take responsibility, rather than a sign to stop. Cris opened Thunder Talks with this view.
principles.quote: self-doubt can also mean you care, that you’re paying attention, that you’re willing to prepare better, to go deeper, and to take responsibility for what you’re about to do.

principles.text: Don't fight self-doubt; learn to relate to it differently so it becomes part of how you grow.
principles.quote: Self-doubt doesn’t disappear, and maybe it’s not even supposed to. It just changes meaning depending on how you choose to relate to it.

principles.text: When you can't guarantee the result, guarantee your involvement and character (a reframe shared by guest Iulia at Thunder Talks).
principles.quote: “If I can’t guarantee the result, I will guarantee my involvement and my character.”

principles.text: Growth is uneven. Sign-up numbers can mislead, and local knowledge only comes from being in enough rooms.
principles.quote: You learn the room by being in it.

principles.text: Culture is not separate from behaviour; look at how people actually act to understand a team's culture.
principles.quote: Culture is behaviour. How you show up, how you speak, how you treat the person next to you, that’s the culture.

principles.text: Exposing the team to different cultures is how Thunder breaks the ceiling of what it thinks is possible, accepting failure along the way.
principles.quote: We believe that exposing ourselves and our team to different cultures and different ways of thinking is how we break the ceiling of what we think is possible.
